title: Magellanic Outflow and Chemistry Survey (MAGOS): Hot Cores in the LMC
question: What are the chemical compositions, molecular tracers, and physical and environmental drivers of chemical diversity (particularly COM-poor chemistry) in hot molecular cores in the subsolar-metallicity Large Magellanic Cloud?

data.sensitivity: continuum rms 0.1-0.2 mJy/beam; spectral rms 0.24-0.30 K

what.value: Catalog of 277 LMC young stellar objects and infrared spectral classifications

evidence.quote: The target sources were selected from the catalog of young stellar objects (YSOs) presented by (cite: Sea09), which includes 277 sources.

what.value: 2MASS, Spitzer SAGE, and Herschel HERITAGE photometric catalogs

evidence.quote: The sources in the (cite: Sea09) catalog include near-infrared and mid-infrared photometric data, which are based on the 2MASS and Spitzer SAGE catalogs (cite: Skr06; Mei06).

Far-infrared data were obtained by performing positional cross-matching between the (cite: Sea09) sources and the Herschel HERITAGE catalog (cite: Mei10), resulting in spectral energy distributions (SEDs) covering the 1–500 $\mu$m range.

recipe.goal: Calculate bolometric luminosities and select target sample
recipe.method: Cross-match YSO catalog with 2MASS, Spitzer SAGE, and Herschel HERITAGE catalogs to build 1-500 um SEDs, integrate fluxes to get bolometric luminosity, and divide luminosity among resolved ALMA continuum components proportional to 850 um flux.
key_parameters: Luminosity bins: 10^4-10^4.5 L_sun, 10^4.5-10^5 L_sun, 10^5-10^5.5 L_sun (10 sources each)
assumptions: Multiple resolved submillimeter components share the infrared luminosity in proportion to their 850 um continuum flux

recipe.goal: Image continuum and spectral lines, and extract source spectra
recipe.method: Subtract continuum with uvcontsub, image continuum and lines with tclean using Briggs robust=0.5 and auto-multithresh, restore line cubes to 0.40'' circular beam, apply primary beam correction with impbcor, and extract spectra and continuum fluxes from 0.41'' (0.1 pc) apertures centered on continuum peaks.
key_parameters: Aperture: 0.41'' diameter circle (0.62'' x 0.41'', PA=65 deg ellipse for Lh09)
Detection criterion: 3 sigma significance and velocity consistency with V_sys; 2 or 3 channels binned for weak lines

recipe.goal: Estimate rotational temperatures and column densities via rotation diagrams and LTE equations
recipe.method: Construct rotation diagrams for species with multiple lines (CH3OH, SO2, 34SO2, CH3OCH3, HCOOCH3, C2H5OH, trans-HCOOH) to fit T_rot and N; for other species, compute LTE column density using assumed T_rot; correct CH3OH and SO2 for optical depth using 13CH3OH and 34SO2 isotopologues where detected.
key_parameters: Hot core classification threshold: T_rot > 100 K
Two-component fit boundary for SO2 and 34SO2: E_u <= 80 K and E_u >= 90 K
assumptions: Optically thin condition, LTE, beam filling factor of unity, and T_rot >> T_bg (T_bg = 2.73 K)
T_rot(SO, SO+) = T_rot(high-T SO2); T_rot(other COMs) = T_rot(CH3OH); T_rot(SiO) = T_rot(high-T SO2 or CH3OH or average) with 50% uncertainty; T_rot(H13CO+) = 30-60 K

recipe.goal: Derive H2 column densities, fractional molecular abundances, and environmental correlations
recipe.method: Calculate N_H2 from 850 um dust continuum brightness using optically thin dust emission formula, compute fractional abundances N(X)/N_H2, and evaluate correlation coefficients between line intensities, abundances, T_rot, FWHM, L_bol, Spitzer IR types, and 24 um surface brightness.
key_parameters: kappa_nu = 1.96 cm^2 g^-1 at 850 um; dust-to-gas mass ratio Z = 0.0027
assumptions: Optically thin 850 um dust continuum; T_d equals T_rot of high-temperature SO2, CH3OH, or their average; 30% uncertainty in N_H2; for Lh09, N_H2 = (8 +/- 4) x 10^23 cm^-2 assumed due to free-free contamination
